title: Rarity
wikitext:
'''Rarity''' is a property found across different types of game content within [[Path of Exile]], including most [[item]]s, [[monster]]s, and [[strongbox]]es. The four rarities are {{c|normal|normal}}, followed by {{c|magic|magic}}, {{c|rare|rare}} and {{c|unique|unique}}. An associated game mechanic that determines the drop rate of higher rarity items is called "Item Rarity". __TOC__ ==Rarity as an item property== ===Normal=== [[File:Goat's Horn 1 Normal.png|thumb|right|upright=1.0|{{c|normal|Normal}} {{il|Goat's Horn}}]] {{c|normal|Normal}} items (also called "base type" items) are the "default" state of items without any [[explicit modifier]]s ([[affixes]]). Some specific base types may have [[implicit modifier]]s. A normal item can be upgraded into a {{c|magic|magic}} item using an {{il|Orb of Transmutation}}, or a {{c|rare|rare}} item using an {{il|Orb of Alchemy}}, which will also add explicit modifiers. Using an {{il|Orb of Chance}} can upgrade a {{c|normal|normal}} item randomly into a {{c|magic|magic}}, {{c|rare|rare}}, or even {{c|unique|unique}} item of the same base type. Using the [[crafting bench]] to craft on a normal item will automatically turn it into a magic item. {{c|magic|Magic}} and {{c|rare|Rare}} items can be reset to a normal state by using a {{il|Orb of Scouring}} (unless the item is [[fractured]]). ===Magic=== [[File:Goat's Horn 2 Magic Transmutation orb.png|thumb|right|upright=1.0|{{c|magic|Magic}} {{il|Goat's Horn}}]] {{c|magic|Magic}} items can have up to two [[affixes]] (one [[prefix]] and one [[suffix]]). The modifiers that can roll are determined by the item's base type and [[item level]], as well as other item properties such as [[Influenced item|Influence]]. The name of the item will include the names of the item's prefix and suffix if present. A magic tem with only one affix can have a second affix added using an {{il|Orb of Augmentation}}. Affixes can be randomly rerolled with an {{il|Orb of Alteration}}. A magic item can be upgraded into a {{c|rare|rare}} item using a {{il|Regal Orb}}. It will retain its current affixes and one new affix will be added. ===Rare=== [[File:Goat's Horn 4 Rare Regal orb.png|thumb|right|upright=1.0|{{c|rare|Rare}} {{il|Goat's Horn}}]] {{c|rare|Rare}} items can have up to six affixes in most cases (three prefixes and three suffixes). Most rare items naturally generate with 4, 5, or 6 affixes at a ratio of 8:3:1 respectively. {{c|rare|Rare}} items are given a [[Rare Item Name Index|randomly generated name]] which are not connected to the item's modifiers. A rare item with less than 6 affixes can gain additional affixes using an {{il|Exalted Orb}}, and it is possible to remove modifiers without reducing the item's rarity using an {{il|Orb of Annulment}}. Affixes can be randomly rerolled with a {{il|Chaos Orb}}. Certain base types, such as [[flask]]s, [[tincture]]s, and [[Relic]]s cannot be {{c|rare|rare}}. Additionally, certain base types such as [[jewel]]s or [[Rogue's equipment]] are limited to 4 explicit modifiers when rare (2 prefix/2 suffix). In some cases, it may be possible to bypass modifier limits, such as through [[Corrupted|corruption]]. ===Unique=== {{main|Unique item}} [[File:Goat's Horn Unique.png|thumb|right|upright=1.0|{{c|unique|Unique}} {{il|Goat's Horn}}]] {{c|unique|[[Unique items]]}} (sometimes referred to as "Legendary" items in other games) are special versions of items with a distinct name, unique 2D and often 3D artwork, a custom set of modifiers instead of random affixes, and a flavour text that introduces more of [[Wraeclast]]'s lore. Unique items are not necessarily stronger or more valuable than rare items; while certain modifiers may be better than those that can randomly roll, other modifiers are exclusive to the unique item and may enable builds or playstyles that are not normally possible otherwise. Unique items are also categorized internally within a [[unique item tier]], ranging from Tier 5 (most common) to Tier 0 (most rare), which again may not necessarily reflect their power or value. Unique items' modifiers cannot be crafted using regular currency as these are specific to the unique item. It is not possible to change the rarity of a unique item other than by [[corrupted|corrupting]] it, which usually has a 25% chance to turn the item into a corrupted rare item. ==Rarity as a monster property== The rarity of a monster grants various multipliers to its base stats. Among the stats affected are [[life]], [[damage]], granted [[experience]] and [[flask]] charges, item quantity and rarity, and a reduced chance to [[fleeing|flee]]. Rarity also causes monsters to drop items with a higher [[item level]]. Magic mobs drop items one level higher than the area, while rare and unique enemies drop items two levels higher. ===Magic monster modifiers=== Increased statistics, and given one [[monster modifier]]. They appear in smaller groups. Magic monsters may also have [[Torment]] and/or [[Delirium]] modifiers. All magic monsters receive the following mods: {{:List of innate magic monster modifiers}} Additionally magic monsters receive a life multiplier based on their level:
{{#cargo_query: |tables=monster_life_scaling |fields=level=Level, CONCAT("+", magic, "%")=Life }}
===Rare monster modifiers=== Greatly increased statistics, and given two to four monster modifiers. They spawn by themselves, but multiple rares may still be close together. Rare monsters may also have [[Torment]], [[Essence]], [[Bestiary]], and/or [[Delirium]] modifiers. All rare monsters receive the following mods: {{:List of innate rare monster modifiers}} Additionally rare monsters receive a life multiplier based on their level:
{{#cargo_query: |tables=monster_life_scaling |fields=level=Level, CONCAT("+", rare, "%")=Life }}
===Unique monster modifiers=== [[Unique Monsters]] that appear in certain areas, including bosses. Some unique monsters like [[Tormented Spirits]] and [[Rogue Exiles]] can spawn in most areas as well. All unique monsters receive the following mods: {{:List of innate unique monster modifiers}} ==Item Rarity (item drop generation)== Random item drops from [[monster]]s and [[chest]]s are determined by selection from a pool of category of possible items called "Drop Pools", which uses the concept of [[weight]]s. The specific Drop Pools that are eligible to roll from depends on the drop's determined rarity (e.g. normal, magic, rare, unique), the selection of which is determined by the "Item Rarity" stat (e.g. {{c|mod|#% increased Rarity of Items Found}}). Rarity stats can apply to four independent vectors: {| class="wikitable" |+ Sources of Item Rarity |- ! Pool || Source || Notes |- | '''Player''' || * Stats from equipped [[item]]s and [[jewel]]s * {{il|Item Rarity Support}} * Player buffs (e.g. {{il|Gold Flask}}, [[Radiant Tempest]], [[Alva]]'s buff in [[The Temple of Atzoatl]]) | * Player IIR/IIQ is the only source of rarity with confirmed diminishing returns. * [[Minion]]s and [[proxies]] use the [[character]]'s IIR/IIQ, plus IIR/IIQ from {{il|Item Rarity Support}}/{{il|Item Quantity Support}} if supported. Rarity stats on the minion itself (e.g. {{il|Animate Guardian}}) are never used, even with {{il|Gravebind}}.https://old.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/xn0vk0/magic_find_with_an_animate_guardian_ez_extra_43/iq1zocu/?context=1 * [[Mercenaries]] use their own IIR stats and do not share with the player. * Player IIR specifically does not affect [[currency]] drops or [[gold]] quantity.https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/4013527 |- | '''Monster''' || * [[Rarity#Monster_rarity|Inherent rarity bonuses]] based on monster's rarity * Hidden monster rarity multipliers * [[Tormented Spirit]]s * [[Covetous Shrine]] (affecting monsters) * [[Wildwood Wisp]]s * [[Sentinel]] empowerment * Other "difficulty and reward" modifiers | * Strongboxes also have an internal rarity similar to monsters. |- | '''Area''' || * [[Map modifier|Map/area modfiers]] (including from [[Shaped Region]]s) * [[Map fragment]]s * [[Atlas passive tree]] * [[Eldritch Altar]]s/[[Memory Altar]]s |- | '''Miscellaneous''' || * [[Partying#Effect_on_loot|Party bonus]] * [[Delirium]] | * Partying does not directly grant IIR, but instead increases the drop rates of higher value items, and acts as a pseudo more multiplier for unique items. * Delirium appears to provides a currently unknown bonus to item rarity to monsters affected by it in some cases, scaled by Deliriousness %. |} Monster Item Rarity is the most important vector for determining the Drop Pools that can roll for each drop. Certain Drop Pools only roll at a certain drop rarity. {| class="wikitable sortable" |+ Known Drop Pools (not a complete list) |- ! Drop Pool !! Normal !! Magic !! Rare !! Unique |- | {{il|Scroll of Wisdom}} || {{yes}} || {{no}} || {{no}} || {{no}} |- | {{il|Portal Scroll}} || {{yes}} || {{no}} || {{no}} || {{no}} |- | Magic Currency * {{il|Orb of Transmutation}} * {{il|Orb of Alteration}} * {{il|Jeweller's Orb}} | {{no}} || {{yes}} || {{no}} || {{no}} |- | Rare Currency * {{il|Orb of Alchemy}} * {{il|Chaos Orb}} * {{il|Divine Orb}} * {{il|Mirror of Kalandra}} | {{no}} || {{no}} || {{yes}} || ? |- | Normal items || {{yes}} || {{no}} || {{no}} || {{no}} |- | Magic items || {{no}} || {{yes}} || {{no}} || {{no}} |- | Rare items || {{no}}|| {{no}} || {{yes}} || {{no}} |- | Unique items || {{no}}|| {{no}}|| {{no}} || {{yes}} |} ===Increased Item Rarity=== In addition to Drop Pool, modifiers to Item Rarity from any vector also affect the chance for more valuable drops to occur. This includes: * '''Unique item tier''': Increases the chance for dropped unique items to be a higher [[unique item tier]]. * '''Divination card rarity''': Increases the chance to drop rarer [[divination card]]s, and prevents certain common divination cards from dropping at very high monster Item Rarity * '''Item Tier''': Increases the chance to drop an item with an Item Tier (e.g. {{c|craftinglife|Unidentified (Tier 5)}}). Player Item Rarity (also known as "magic find" or "MF") also contributes more heavily to these effects than to Drop Pool. Player Item Rarity does not affect currency drops. Player Item Rarity also does not affect items dropped by [[chest]]s or from deterministic sources such as Item Templates (tile loot). For a list of items that grant Player Item Rarity, see: [[List of items that alter Item Rarity]]. ===="Item Tier"==== Item Tiers are drop enabled at certain [[drop level]] thresholds, starting from [[Act 6]]. Values range from Tier 2 to Tier 5. Only items that have a Rarity as a property (e.g. [[equipment]]) can have Item Tiers. Items with Item Tiers have the following effects: * Item Tiers affect the [[Modifier Tier Rating]] of magic and rare items when identified. It does not affect modifiers changed after the item is identified, such as through [[crafting]]. * Item Tiers affect the chance for higher level base types (e.g. for weapons or armour), chance to have [[quality]] and higher values of quality, and the chance to have more [[gem socket]]s and [[link]]s. * Tier 5 items have a chance to drop with +1 to [[item level]]. * Tier 5 items have a chance to drop as [[fractured]] magic items. * Magic or rare items that are a certain Unidentified Tier or above can instead drop as pseudo-exclusive core drop pool base types instead: ** Tier 3+: *** {{il|Artillery Quiver}} *** {{il|Bone Helmet}} *** {{il|Spiked Gloves}}, {{il|Gripped Gloves}}, {{il|Fingerless Silk Gloves}}, {{il|Apothecary's Gloves}} *** [[Two-Toned Boots]] (three variants), {{il|Fugitive Boots}} *** {{il|Vermillion Ring}}, {{il|Cerulean Ring}}, {{il|Steel Ring}}, {{il|Opal Ring}}, {{il|Iolite Ring}} *** {{il|Marble Amulet}}, {{il|Blue Pearl Amulet}}, {{il|Seaglass Amulet}} *** {{il|Crystal Belt}}, {{il|Vanguard Belt}} ** Tier 5: *** {{il|Manifold Ring}}, {{il|Helical Ring}}, {{il|Cogwork Ring}}, {{il|Geodesic Ring}}, {{il|Ratcheting Ring}}, {{il|Composite Ring}}, *** {{il|Astrolabe Amulet}}, {{il|Simplex Amulet}}, {{il|Focused Amulet}} *** {{il|Stygian Vise}}, {{il|Cord Belt}} Items in [[Ruthless mode]] cannot have Item Tiers. ==Version history== {{Version history table header}} {{Version history table row|3.30.0| * Fundamentally changed how Items are generated in Path of Exile. * Previously, if a monster drops an item it rolls its "Rarity" (Normal, Magic, Rare or Unique) based on the monster's Item Rarity. If the "Rarity" was not Unique it would then pick from a list of Drop Pools such as Weapons, Rings, Scrolls of Wisdom, Skills Gems, Currency etc to select a specific item to drop. * For example, if the selected "Rarity" was Rare, and the selected Drop Pool was Weapons, then it would generate a random weapon and because the "Rarity" was Rare the weapon would generate as a Rare item. If the selected Drop Pool was Scrolls of Wisdom, then it would generate a Scroll of Wisdom. In this case the monster having more Item Rarity was mostly meaningless as if the selected "Rarity" was Normal, Magic or Rare the item generated would still be a Scroll of Wisdom. * Because of the above, Magic monsters (which have much higher Item Rarity compared to Normal monsters) had 50% less chance to drop items that can't have rarity, such as Currency or Skill Gems, while Rare and Uniques had 80% less chance. This was to prevent the experience of killing a difficult boss and having most of the items that dropped not care about the Item Rarity of that boss. * Item Rarity on monsters and chests has changed to now affect which Drop Pools can be selected. For example, the Scrolls of Wisdom and Portal Scrolls Drop Pools now can only be selected if the generated "Rarity" was normal. This means as monsters have more Item Rarity they will drop fewer Scrolls of Wisdom and Portal Scrolls. * Currency item Drop Pools have been split into a Magic Currency (such as Orbs of Transmutation, Orbs of Alteration, Jeweller's Orbs) and Rare Currency (such as Orbs of Alchemy, Chaos Orbs, Divine Orbs and Mirrors of Kalandra). Magic Currency can only generate if the selected "Rarity" was Magic, and Rare Currency can only generate if the selected "Rarity" was Rare. What this amounts to is the more Item Rarity a monster has, the better the Currency items it drops. * Because high Item Rarity on Monsters now excludes common currencies and increases the chance for valuable currencies, we have removed 50% less chance to drop items that can't have rarity from Magic Monsters, and 80% less from Rare and Unique monsters. As a result, a much greater percentage of valuable currency items you find will now be coming from Rare and Unique Monsters. * Rare and Magic Monster modifiers no longer add Quantity of Items Dropped to Monsters. * The amount of Rarity of Items Dropped granted by Rare and Magic Monster modifiers has been increased. * Rare Monsters now have slightly more inherent Item Quantity. * In Act 6 onwards, Rare and Magic Items now have a change to generate with an Item Tier, ranging from 2 to 5. The tier of the item influences the modifier tier rating on the item when it is identified, higher tier resulting in higher modifier tier rating. * In addition, Item Tier will influence the chance for the item to be a higher level base type (for Weapons and Armours), chance to have Quality, chance for higher Quality, and chance to have more Sockets and Socket links. * Item Rarity on Monsters affects the chance for Rare and Magic items to have Item Tiers. * At higher levels, Item Rarity on Monsters affects the chance for Uniques that drop to be rarer Uniques, when a Unique item would drop. * Items in Ruthless do not have Item Tiers. * Decreased the efficacy of player Item Rarity on finding Magic, Rare and Unique Rarity items. Player Item Rarity now affects the chance to find Tiered Magic and Rare items. * Tier 5 items have a chance to drop with +1 to Item Level. * Tier 5 items have a chance to drop as Fractured Magic items. }} {{Version history table row|3.25.0| * The way that the Quantity and Rarity of items dropped from extra content has been changed. Generally we have added item Quantity or Rarity bonuses to a number of mechanics, such as Essences, or Delirium. On top of that we have added drops back to some leagues where it wasn't present before, like Ultimatum. In general the philosophy here is that if you are killing monsters you get loot, and if they are more difficult, you should get more and better loot. *A major change we have made alongside the above is that we have changed a lot of the quantity and rarity bonuses on monsters to prevent things multiplying out of control at the very top end. }} {{Version history table row|1.0.0f| * Fixed an extremely rare bug where too many unique items could drop from a monster outside of the Albino Rhoa Event. }} {{Version history table row|0.8.6| * Fixed item rarity calculations. "Increased item rarity" now works properly. }} {{Version history table row|0.8.3| * Nerfed item quantity [[mod]]s. }} {{Version history table row|0.6.8| * Nerfed "increased item quantity" stat by 50%. }} {{Version history table end}} ==References== {{reflist|refs= {{cite web|author=Mark_GGG|date=February 16, 2012|title=For the love of god, please, rework DEXTERITY.
